body:
Suresh ji, good question — here's a simple shape for a corporate bulk thali package:

🍛 Corporate Thali Plan (for offices in Indiranagar)
• Min 10 thalis/order, ₹149 each (same as your lunch thali)
• Free delivery on orders above ₹1,500
• Order before 10:30 AM, delivered by 12:30 PM
• Weekly billing option for offices that order daily
• Add-ons: curd, extra roti, dessert at ₹20/₹10/₹30

Why now: 'weekday lunch thali' searches are up 34% YoY, mostly office folks 25-45. Your thali already does 18 orders/day, and 22 positive thali reviews in the last 30 days — this just adds a predictable bulk channel.

Shall I draft a one-page menu + WhatsApp ordering link you can send to 5 nearby offices?
rationale: Merchant asked what a corporate bulk thali package would look like. Message answers directly with a concrete package structure, uses his existing ₹149 thali and performance data (18 orders/day, 22 positive reviews), adds the weekday lunch thali trend (+34% YoY) as a timely hook, and ends with one clear next step. Scope is merchant, so send_as is vera. Code-mix Hindi-English matches merchant language preferences.

body: Dr. Meera, while I finish those whitening/aligner posts — ek quick compliance heads-up. DCI has revised radiograph dose limits: max dose per IOPA exposure drops from 1.5 mSv to 1.0 mSv, effective 15 Dec 2026 (DCI circular 2026-11-04). E-speed film passes at the new limit; D-speed doesn't. Digital RVG sensors are unaffected. So before the deadline, it's worth auditing your X-ray setup and documenting E-speed or RVG in your SOPs. Want me to send a 5-point pre-audit checklist you can share with your radiology tech? Reply YES.
rationale: Merchant-scope compliance trigger; sent as Vera. Message references the DCI circular and deadline, uses clinical vocabulary, ties to the prior conversation about drafting posts, and ends with a single binary CTA for a checklist.
